leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 files prefer a single-achievement B021 prize for Daniel J. Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov, with a citation anchored in GLP-1 physiology and the active peptide form that enabled incretin-based therapies. Members give the same scientific reasons: a complete chain from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect to the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and receptor biology, then to drugs with large independent outcome trials. Members state that the identical opening ranks are not their argument. What is not shared is how much weight the unresolved attribution questions carry: the Mojsov versus Habener priority dispute, and the exclusion of Lotte Bjerre Knudsen under the three-person cap. All six name both as the main reservation; none moves Knudsen into the configuration. Citation wording differs slightly across files, and the shortlist does not show whether members would accept a physiology-centred citation as final.

areas_of_agreement: All six members prefer the same B021 trio (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov) as their round-1 configuration, and none proposes a multi-part prize as the preferred configuration.

Members agree that B021 is mature: the mechanism is settled, the interpretation has been stable for decades, and independent outcome trials across several drug classes show glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal effects.
Members agree that the three-person cap forces Knudsen's drug-development role out of the B021 configuration, and that this is a policy choice to state openly rather than a scientific finding.
Five members list B033 (CAR-T) and B044 (optogenetics) as alternatives; Wahren-Herlenius lists B033 and B032 (TNF blockade). B033 is an alternative for all six.

For B033, members who address it (Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius, El-Manira, Svenningsson) agree that Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy is a different achievement from CAR-specific design, and that Eshhar's absence from the credited names is a fairness problem under any configuration.

Members who comment on B042 (SMN2 antisense) and B052 (unfolded protein response) accept the clean two-person attribution of both but describe them as later candidates, not competitors to B021 this year.
scientific_disputes: Whether a methodological tool (B044, optogenetics) fits the Physiology or Medicine remit as strongly as a disease-linked therapy or mechanism. El-Manira and Perlmann keep it as an alternative; Sandberg calls it a methods prize with contested allocation; Wahren-Herlenius would not oppose it in a two-part prize but would not support it as the single anchor.

Whether TNF blockade (B032) is an independent discovery or the clinical translation of TNF biology and antibody engineering done by others. Wahren-Herlenius cites over twenty-five years of confirmation and a clean pair; El-Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg and Svenningsson raise the translation objection.

Whether B052 (UPR) is a stronger prize on scientific generality than its indirect clinical translation allows. Perlmann says the UPR is a general principle of intracellular signalling and the better scientific case than SMA antisense; Linnarsson and El-Manira rate its translation as too indirect to rank it above B033 or B044.
Whether B042 (SMN2 antisense) is a general platform or a single-disease drug story. Members note that SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) lies outside the credited names.

Whether the cGAS-STING pathway (B015), with no demonstrated clinical benefit yet, rests on mechanism alone. Wahren-Herlenius supports a Chen and Barber pairing as the cleanest version; El-Manira and Perlmann treat it as a later candidate.
attribution_disputes: B021: priority for identifying the active truncated GLP-1(7-36) peptide is contested between Mojsov and the Habener group, and Habener is outside the credited names. Several members state that their account of the history is partly recalled and not independently verified.

B021: whether Knudsen should displace one of the three physiology names. Perlmann calls her the most natural fourth name; Svenningsson says that if translation must be recognised the choice is between Knudsen and Mojsov and he leans towards keeping Mojsov; Wahren-Herlenius says any replacement should rest on an explicit rationale, most plausibly where priority is most disputed, not on default; Linnarsson and Perlmann would keep her out to preserve the line between physiology and industrial development.

B033: the chimeric-receptor concept originates with Eshhar, who is not among the credited names. Members differ on whether June and Sadelain alone (Linnarsson, Perlmann after reconsideration, Wahren-Herlenius, El-Manira on reflection) is a defensible pair or only reduces the problem; Sandberg ranks it second but not as a clean attribution.

B044: six credited names against a three-person cap. Proposals in the files differ: Boyden, Deisseroth and Hegemann; Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann. Members dispute whether the prize should reward channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) or neuronal implementation (Boyden, Deisseroth), and whether Miesenbock is left out unfairly.
B032: Feldmann and Maini are described as a clean two-person attribution, but members note upstream TNF and antibody work by others (Old, Cerami, Beutler and industrial teams).
B015: Chen and Barber are described as the cleanest pairing; Ishikawa, Wu and Sun are in the credited list, and a three-person cap would require a choice.
maturity_disputes: B021 is treated by all six as mature, with outcome evidence from multiple drug classes; no member argues it is premature.

B033: Wahren-Herlenius raises long-term safety, secondary malignancy and activity beyond haematological cancers as reasons to wait or to narrow the credit; Linnarsson calls it an equally clear and arguably more novel therapeutic modality.
B044: Wahren-Herlenius notes that clinical translation of optogenetics is only starting; El-Manira describes both optogenetics and the UPR as mature, with optogenetics having wider reach.
B042: Sandberg and El-Manira describe the antisense platform as younger and a later candidate than B021; Linnarsson would revisit it after a longer record.
B032: members who comment treat the over twenty-five years of clinical confirmation as a strength, not a weakness; the dispute is about what the discovery was, not about maturity.
B015: the lack of demonstrated clinical benefit is the stated reason for placing it as a later candidate.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: El-Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored stem-cell-derived dopamine neuron paper with Perlmann, and field overlap with optogenetics as a user of such tools; no documented tie to any credited optogenetics candidate.
Perlmann discloses co-authorship with Svenningsson and one paper with El-Manira; neither relates to the shortlisted candidates or credited names.
Svenningsson discloses co-authorship with Perlmann on dopamine neuron topics and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard, who is not a candidate.

Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen (not candidates) and shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation, plus topical closeness of his single-cell and RNA processing research to B042, with no documented tie to Krainer or Bennett.

Wahren-Herlenius discloses field familiarity with B032 (TNF blockade) and B015 (cGAS-STING) and a risk of bias toward them; no documented co-authorship, institutional tie or relationship with any candidate.
Linnarsson reports no specific conflict; his documented link to spatial transcriptomics and brain atlases does not connect to the shortlisted candidates.
No member reports a recusal-level conflict for any shortlisted ballot.
questions_for_round2: Can four members accept a physiology-centred B021 citation that openly leaves out drug development, and if the committee instead wishes to recognise Knudsen, which of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov yields and on what stated ground?

What evidence in the supplied record settles the Mojsov versus Habener priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, and if it cannot be settled, should Mojsov remain in the configuration or should the citation be reworded to avoid a priority claim?

Should the final configuration be a single-achievement B021 prize, or is there a second part (B033, B044 or B032) that at least four members would support, given that a three-person cap per prize would then force a smaller B021 group?
If B033 is pursued, can the committee defend a June and Sadelain pair without Eshhar, and does anyone still support Rosenberg as a third laureate?

If B044 is pursued, which three of the six credited names and which citation wording (discovery of channelrhodopsin versus neuronal implementation) would members accept, and can any split be defended without misrepresenting priority?
Should B032 (Feldmann and Maini) be treated as an independent discovery or as translation of earlier TNF biology, and do members who ranked it low accept that distinction as stated?
Do members hold B042 and B052 to the same standards of clarity of credit and translational impact as the leading candidates, and would any member move either into a configuration this year?
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 files show full convergence on B021 with the same three laureates, with the main contested questions being attribution (Mojsov and Habener, Knudsen, Eshhar) and whether to add a second achievement. Alternatives cluster on B033 and B044, with B032 raised by one member. Round 2 should test whether the physiology-centred configuration holds when its stated weaknesses are weighed against the alternatives, rather than rely on the unanimity of the openings, which members have said they do not treat as an argument.
